<reason>Both sides argued at a high level and the clash narrowed cleanly. CON (A) was the more quotable debater and landed the sharpest single hit: forcing PRO to choose between stranding a newborn (Baby Manji as policy) and admitting the passport threat is empty, then exploiting PRO's "the child comes home" answer to revive the price-competition objection and the "respectable storefront" framing. But CON's own affirmative alternative absorbed the heavier, better-targeted pressure. Asked what prohibition gives the woman already pregnant in Tbilisi, CON honestly answered "there is no mechanism, and I don't claim one," resting instead on unquantified volume reduction — and CON's volume-reduction levers (home-state broker liability, payment processors, criminal exposure) are the same home-jurisdiction levers CON insisted cannot make standards bite, a symmetry PRO exposed with "if judges blink at my friction, they blink at your fines." PRO also retained concrete, home-domiciled instruments (escrow in licensed banks, panel counsel that can be struck off, home-licensed insurers, revocable listing with market-access loss) which CON damaged but did not eliminate; CON's best counter — that the only credible complainant is a dependent surrogate abroad — cut into revocation without killing escrow or insurance. PRO's closing risk-asymmetry weighing ("if I'm wrong she still has a contract; if you're wrong she has nothing, and cannot go to a court or hospital without confessing to a crime") converted the "leaky mechanism versus no mechanism" comparison into the cleanest voting reason on the table, and it defended the motion as written. CON's closing reframe — that an unmeetable condition is permission, not a safeguard — was elegant and nearly sufficient, but it never gave the third-party reader a protected person under prohibition. CON also took a small execution cost for the clipped Rebuttal 2 weighing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q2 ("name the mechanism that gives a surrogate in Tbilisi escrow or post-delivery coverage under your ban") and CON's candid "there is no mechanism, and I don't claim one." The honesty was creditable, but it handed PRO the decisive comparative — identifiable protections versus an unprovable count of women never recruited — which PRO then weighted with the risk-asymmetry framing in closing. CON's counter-exploitation of "the child comes home" was the second-best moment, but it damaged PRO's deterrence rather than restoring CON's own protective story.</best_rebuttal>
